He was selected 11th overall by the Bulls in the [[2024 NBA draft]]. ==Early life and high school career== Buzelis was born in [[Chicago]] on October 13, 2004. Both of his parents played basketball professionally in [[Lithuania]] before immigrating to the [[United States]] and settling in the Chicago area, where Buzelis was born and raised.{{Cite web |last=Fowler |first=Chapel |date=May 17, 2022 |title=UNC basketball, Hubert Davis target 5-star recruit Matas Buzelis |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/05/17/unc-basketball-hubert-davis-recruiting-matas-buzelis/9673176002/ |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]}} During his childhood, Buzelis attended [[gymnastics]] school with his brother and sister. Later in the same school, he attended [[Swimming (sport)|swimming]] and had the best results among under-10 and under-12 [[breaststroke]] swimmers in the state of [[Illinois]].{{cite web |last=Urbonas |first=Donatas |date=2021-02-05 |title=Buzelių DNR: už Atlanto auga įžaidėjas, kokio Lietuvoje nesutiksi |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/buzeliu-dnr-uz-atlanto-auga-izaidejas-kokio-lietuvoje-nesutiksi-875-1445756 |access-date=17 August 2023 |website=[[15min.lt]] |language=lt}} Buzelis initially attended [[Hinsdale Central High School]] in suburban [[Hinsdale, Illinois|Hinsdale]] and played on their sophomore team as a freshman.{{cite web |last=Narang |first=Bobby |date=October 18, 2020 |title=Future Illini? Hinsdale Central sophomore Matas Buzelis weighs an offer from Illinois — while waiting to play first varsity game |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/hinsdale/sports/ct-dhd-recruiting-notes-hinsdale-central-matas-buzelis-tl-1022-20201018-jpvizepygzc2tbmb65phgfsque-story.html |access-date=February 17, 2023 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}} He transferred to [[Brewster Academy]], a boarding school in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]], midway through the start of the first semester of his sophomore year after Hinsdale Central's basketball season was postponed due to concerns related to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last=Henricksen |first=Joe |date=November 3, 2021 |title=City/Suburban Hoops Report: The search for a No. 1 in 2023, two-sport powerhouses, prep school threats |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2021/11/3/22761223/high-school-basketball-asa-thomas-jj-taylor-mikey-williams |access-date=February 17, 2023 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]}} As a junior, Buzelis was named the 2022 New Hampshire Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 11.4 points, 5.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite press release |title=BREWSTER ACADEMY STUDENT-ATHLETE NAMED GATORADE NEW HAMPSHIRE BOYS BASKETBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR |date=March 16, 2022 |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/poy/assets/writable/68460/2022_BBB_MBuzelis.pdf |access-date=February 17, 2023}} He was also selected to play for Team World in the 2022 [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last=Vecenie |first=Sam |date=February 14, 2023 |title=Bronny James, DJ Wagner, 'JuJu' Watkins headline Nike Hoop Summit rosters |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4200387/2023/02/14/bronny-james-juju-watkins-nike-hoop-summit/ |access-date=February 17, 2023 |work=[[The New York Times]]}} Buzelis transferred to [[Sunrise Christian Academy]] in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]], before the start of his senior year.{{cite web |last=Bossi |first=Eric |date=October 6, 2022 |title=Sunrise Christian has reloaded for the 2022-23 season |url=https://247sports.com/Article/College-Basketball-recruiting-Sunrise-Christian-reloads-Miro-Little-Mikel-Brown-Matas-Buzelis-Scotty-Middleton-Layden-Blocker-194856336/ |access-date=February 17, the free throw line.{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=2022-23 MaxPreps All-America Team: Cameron Boozer of Columbus headlines high school basketball's |website=gleague.nba.com}} ===Chicago Bulls (2024–present)=== ====2024–2025 season==== Buzelis was selected with the 11th overall pick by the [[Chicago Bulls]] during the [[2024 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Poe |first=Julia |date=June 26, 2024 |title=Bulls pick Matas Buzelis at No. 11 in 2024 NBA draft |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2024/06/26/chicago-bulls-matas-buzelis-2024-nba-draft/ |access-date=June 27, 2024 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Sam |author-link=Sam Smith (sportswriter) |date=June 27, 2024 |title=Matas Buzelis brings 'size, athleticism, versatility' to Bulls |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/matas-buzelis-brings-size-athleticism-versatility-to-bulls |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} Buzelis reportedly worked his way as a projected top 5 in the pre-draft process as teams were interested in his size and feel for the game putting him as a top 5 pick commonly to the [[Detroit Pistons]] who decided to go with Ignite teammate [[Ron Holland (basketball)|Ron Holland]]. Other teams passed on Buzelis dropping him to his hometown Bulls.{{Cite web |title=Is Matas Buzelis Most Realistic Option for Pistons? {{!}} Highlights and Live Video from Bleacher Report |url=https://bleacherreport.com/videos/575318-is-matas-buzelis-most-realistic-option-for-pistons |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240728220559/https://bleacherreport.com/videos/575318-is-matas-buzelis-most-realistic-option-for-pistons |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 28, 2024 |access-date=2024-07-28 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}{{Cite magazine |last=Grasso |first=Justin |date=2024-06-27 |title=Popular Detroit Pistons NBA Draft Prospect Lands With Rival Team |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pistons/news/popular-detroit-pistons-nba-draft-prospect-lands-with-rival-team-01j1ag53tw11 |access-date=2024-07-28 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en-US}} He signed a rookie-scale contract with the Bulls on July 2, 2024.{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=July 3, 2024 |title=Bulls Sign Matas Buzelis To Rookie Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/bulls-sign-matas-buzelis-to-rookie-contract.html |access-date=July 3, 2024 |website=HoopsRumors.com}}{{Better source needed|date=April 2026}} Buzelis made his NBA debut on October 23, 2024, in a 123–111 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |date=November 1, 2024 |title=Chicago Bulls at New Orleans Pelicans Box Score, October 23, 2024 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410230NOP.html |access-date=November 1, 2024 |website=BasketballRef}} On January 20, 2025, he committed to the [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] during the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game|2025 All-Star weekend]], becoming the first Lithuanian player to do so. He also became the first Bulls player to participate in the contest since [[Tyrus Thomas]] in [[2007 NBA All-Star Game|2007]].{{cite web|date=February 4, 2025 |title=Matas Buzelis to participate in NBA Slam Dunk Contest |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/matas-buzelis-to-participate-in-nba-slam-dunk-contest |access-date=February 7, 2025|website=NBA.com}} On February 4, Buzelis scored 24 points while shooting 10-for-10 from the field in a 133–124 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |last=Cowley |first=Joe |date=February 4, 2025 |title=Bulls rookie Matas Buzelis announces his arrival with breakout game |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls/2025/02/04/bulls-rookie-matas-buzelis-announces-arrival-breakout-game |access-date=February 5, 2025 |website=Chicago Sun-Times}} In addition to participation in the NBA Slam Dunk Contest, Buzelis was also selected to play for [[Mitch Richmond]]'s team during the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game#Rising Stars Challenge|2025 Rising Stars Challenge]], where his team was eliminated in the semifinal 40–39.{{cite web |title=Matas Buzelis selected to the 2025 Castrol Rising Stars Game |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/matas-buzelis-selected-to-the-2025-castrol-rising-stars-game |website=NBA.com}} On March 22, he put up a career-high 31 points in a 146–115 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|date=March 22, 2025 |title=After looking like he hit rookie wall, Bulls' Matas Buzelis hits back |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls/2025/03/23/after-rookie-wall-bulls-matas-buzelis-hit-back |access-date=March 22, 2025|website=Chicago Sun-Times}} On March 29, Buzelis scored 28 points, grabbed nine rebounds, dished out six assists against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and became the third Bulls rookie to achieve such game statistics, the other two being [[Michael Jordan]] and [[Charles Oakley]].{{cite web |title=M.Buzelio spindesys Čikagoje – gerino ir kartojo šūsnį asmeninių rekordų |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/nba/m-buzelio-spindesys-cikagoje-gerino-ir-kartojo-susni-asmeniniu-rekordu-1130-2421770 |website=[[15min.lt]] |access-date=30 March 2025 |language=lt}} On April 4, Buzelis put up his first career double-double with 12 points and 12 rebounds in a 118–113 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/chicago-bulls/bulls-news-billy-donovan-applauds-matas-buzelis-mindset-first-career-double-double|title=Bulls' Billy Donovan applauds Matas Buzelis' mindset after first career double-double|website=ClutchPoints|last=White|first=Scotty|date=April 4, 2025|access-date=April 4, 2025}} When his playing time increased in the second half of his first NBA season and Buzelis started in 31 games, his averages were 13 points (47.3 percent from the field) and 4.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Jonas Valanciunas Shares Bold Proclamation On Bulls' Matas Buzelis |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bulls/news/jonas-valanciunas-shares-bold-proclamation-on-bulls-matas-buzelis-01k7mdw9tv2v |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=15 October 2025}} His debut season in the NBA ended when the Bulls in the [[2025 NBA play-in tournament]] lost the first game 90–109 to the Miami Heat and failed to qualify for the [[2025 NBA playoffs]].{{cite web |title=Miami Heat knock out Chicago Bulls as Dallas Mavericks set-up Memphis Grizzlies tie |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/basketball/articles/cpdz971g7pvo |website=[[BBC]] |access-date=23 May 2026 |date=17 April 2025}} On May 20, 2025, Buzelis was included to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].{{cite web|title=Stephon Castle, Zaccharie Risacher headline NBA All-Rookie First Team|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2024-25-all-rookie-teams-announced|website=NBA.com|date=May 20, 2025}} ====2025–2026 season==== Buzelis began his [[2025–26 NBA season|second NBA season]] with a dominating performance of 21 points, 6 rebounds, 3 blocks and together with [[Nikola Vučević]] (28 points) led the Bulls to a season-opening 115–111 victory versus the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |title=Vucevic and Buzelis lead Bulls in Season Opening win over Pistons 115-111 |url=https://bulls.com/news/vucevic-and-buzelis-lead-bulls-in-season-opening-win-over-pistons-115-110 |website=Bulls.com |date=October 23, 2025}} When the Bulls traded their long-term players [[Nikola Vučević]], [[Coby White]], and [[Ayo Dosunmu]] just before the NBA trade deadline, Buzelis's role in the team further increased and he became Bulls' leading scorer.{{cite web |last1=Logan |first1=Stacy |title=Matas Buzelis Will Break Out Post All-Star Break |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/matas-buzelis-break-post-star-223414962.html |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=February 16, 2026}} On February 13, Buzelis was selected to play for the [[Vince Carter]]'s team during the [[2026 NBA All-Star Game#Rising Stars Challenge|2026 Rising Stars Challenge]] and his team won the tournament.{{cite web |title=Matas Buzelis' 3rd Rising Stars Game is a Reminder of Much Higher Expectations |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bulls/onsi/news/matas-buzelis-3rd-rising-stars-game-much-higher-expectations-13 |website=Sports Illustrated |date=13 February 2026}} On February 21, Buzelis achieved a new career-high by [[Block (basketball)|blocking]] six shots, along with scoring 15 points, grabbing six rebounds, making two steals, and dishing out three assists, however the Bulls lost the game 126–110 to the Detroit Pistons.{{cite web |title=3 Takeaways & Player Grades: Bulls Drop Eighth Straight in Loss to Pistons (126-110) |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bulls/onsi/news/bulls-drop-eighth-straight-in-loss-to-pistons-126-110-01kj1m8dxytb |website=Sports Illustrated |date=22 February 2026}} On February 24, Buzelis set a new career-high in scoring with 32 points against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], however the Bulls lost the game 131–99.{{cite web |title=Bulls' Matas Buzelis: Logs career highs in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-matas-buzelis-logs-career-highs-in-loss/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |date=25 February 2026}} On March 10, Buzelis set another career-high by scoring 41 points, along with six rebounds, two steals, two assists, two blocks, and led the Bulls to a 130–124 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web |title=Bulls' Matas Buzelis: Records first career 40-point game |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-matas-buzelis-records-first-career-40-point-game/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=March 11, 2026 |date=March 11, 2026}} He became only the third Bulls player in history to score at least 40 points being 21 years old or younger, the other two being Michael Jordan and [[Elton Brand]].{{cite web |title=Po karjeros vakaro – Buzelio kreipimasis į Dievą, trenerio pagyros ir atskleista tėvo pamoka |url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-242828-po-karjeros-vakaro-buzelio-kreipimasis-i-dieva-trenerio-pagyros-ir-atskleista-tevo-pamoka.html |website=BasketNews.lt |access-date=11 March 2026 |language=lt}} Moreover, he matched [[Linas Kleiza]]'s second-highest scoring performance for a Lithuanian player in the NBA and was just one point away from [[Domantas Sabonis]]' all-time scoring record of 42 points.{{cite web |title=Karjeros pasirodymą surengęs Buzelis taikėsi į Lietuvos NBA rezultatyvumo rekordą |url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-242820-karjeros-pasirodyma-surenges-buzelis-taikesi-i-lietuvos-nba-rezultatyvumo-rekorda.html |website=BasketNews.lt |access-date=March 11, 2026 |language=lt}} Buzelis role in the team during his second NBA season significantly increased, his scoring input nearly doubled, however the Bulls finished 12th in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] and lost all chances to qualify for the [[2026 NBA playoffs]].{{cite web |title=Bulls fall to Thunder 131-113, Donovan talks reality of missing postseason |url=https://bulls.com/news/bulls-fall-to-thunder-131-113-donovan-talks-reality-of-missing-postseason |website=[[Chicago Bulls]] |date=28 March 2026 |access-date=23 May 2026}} ==National team career== 2.1|| 14.3 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Buzelis's maternal grandfather, Arvydas Jankauskas, is a former basketball player and coach, while his paternal grandfather, Petras Buzelis, also is a former basketball player who debuted in [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] at 19 years old, later becoming Žalgiris Kaunas's captain and winning six Lithuanian League titles and three [[USSR Premier Basketball League]] bronze medals. One of Buzelis's grandmothers, Elena Buzelienė, is an all-time great Lithuanian [[handball]] player who won two European Champions Cups. Buzelis's mother, Kristina Jankauskaitė, played for Lithuanian youth basketball national teams and was one of the most promising basketball players of her generation. Buzelis's father, Aidas Buzelis, is a former basketball player who played for multiple [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] clubs and also worked as a [[Physical therapy|physiotherapist]] of the [[Lithuania men's national basketball team]].{{cite web |date=26 August 2019 |title=Rinktinės masažuotojas – apie Kuzminsko ausis ir kūno "įjungimą" |url=https://www.delfi.lt/krepsinis/naujienos/rinktines-masazuotojas-apie-kuzminsko-ausis-ir-kuno-ijungima-82072141 |access-date=17 August 2023 |work=[[DELFI]] |language=lt}} Buzelis speaks [[Lithuanian language|Lithuanian]] in addition to English.{{cite web |last=Urbonas |first=Donatas |date=February 19, 2023 |title=MVP tapęs Matas Buzelis – apie žaidimą Lietuvos rinktinėje ir galingą duetą |url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-185403-mvp-tapes-matas-buzelis-apie-zaidima-lietuvos-rinktineje-ir-galinga-dueta.html |access-date=July 1, 2024 |website=[[BasketNews|BasketNews.lt]] |language=lt}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{FIBA|new_id=321406|name=Matas Buzelis}} {{Chicago Bulls current roster}} {{2024 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Buzelis, Matas}} [[Category:2004 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:American people of Lithuanian descent]] [[Category:Basketball players from Chicago]] [[Category:Brewster Academy alumni]] [[Category:Chicago Bulls draft picks]] [[Category:Chicago Bulls players]] [[Category:Lithuanian men's basketball players]] [[Category:21st-century Lithuanian sportsmen]] [[Category:NBA G League Ignite players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Windy City Bulls players]] [[Category:Sunrise Christian Academy alumni]]
